Name: Medicenna Therapeutics Corp.
Description:
Medicenna is a clinical-stage immunotherapy company pioneering next-generation Superkines - engineered cytokines designed to overcome the limitations of other cytokines and unlock new treatment opportunities in oncology, immunology, and inflammatory diseases. 

Our mission is to develop life-changing immunotherapies that transform people's lives and deliver the best possible patient outcomes.

Our SuperkineTM BiSKITTM and T-MASKTM platforms create novel and highly selective Superkines with best-in-class potential and/or first-in-class features, leveraging validated biology and innovative protein and antibody engineering.

Our lead therapies in development are: 

Bizaxofusp: A Phase-3 ready immunotherapy for the deadliest form of brain cancer, glioblastoma. This is a truly aggressive & devastating disease for patients who typically live 6-9 months at relapse, with no new therapies in decades. Medicenna's program showed doubling of median overall survival in the Phase 2b trial, bringing hope and months of meaningful time to patients with brain cancer.

Medicenna's IL-2 program is a best-in-class IL-2 agonist for metastatic/advanced cancers that have failed other therapies. It is currently being evaluated in a global Phase 1/2 study. This class of therapies has significant potential for patients with many forms of cancer as it trains and builds your immune system to fight off cancer.

Medicenna's most advanced clinical stage program is a PD-1 x IL-2 bispecific, which aims to target cancers which express IL-13Rα2. These cancers do not typically respond to other therapies so there is a large unmet need for approximately ~2M patients annually every year.

Medicenna also has early stage programs in development for autoimmune diseases and chronic inflammatory diseases like asthma and COPD.

Name: Satellos Bioscience
Description: Satellos is a clinical-stage drug development company advancing SAT-3247, a first-of-its-kind, orally administered small molecule therapy designed to enhance the body’s natural muscle repair and regeneration process in degenerative muscle diseases. SAT-3247 is being evaluated as a potentially disease-modifying treatment, initially for DMD, in two Phase 2 clinical trials: BASECAMP in pediatrics and TRAILHEAD in adults. SAT-3247 targets AAK1, a protein that is a key regulator of the body’s natural muscle repair and regeneration biology, which Satellos discovered is disrupted in DMD and other degenerative conditions. By inhibiting AAK1, SAT-3247 is designed to re-establish a critical biochemical signal needed to guide this process, in a dystrophin-independent manner. This mechanistic feature offers SAT-3247 the potential for broad applicability as either a stand-alone treatment to potentially enhance muscle and function, or as adjunctive therapy alongside other approaches. Satellos has identified additional degenerative muscle diseases where enhancing muscle repair and regeneration may have therapeutic benefit and plans to pursue these opportunities in future clinical development.

Name: Raven Biotech Inc.
Description:
Raven Biotech’s stand-alone Methanol Sensor provides reliable, on-line control of methanol concentration in cultures of Pichia pastoris or other methlotrophic organisms, allowing fast and efficient optimization of recombinant protein production. Accurate regulation of the methanol concentration is necessary to maintain induction and prevent the accumulation of methanol to cytotoxic levels.
In the past, the dissolved oxygen spike method has been used to estimate the methanol concentration. This technique, however, exposes the cells to potentially non-inducing levels of methanol and cannot be easily implement with Mut- clones or with mixed substrate feeds.

Raven’s Methanol Sensor overcomes these limitations, giving accurate monitoring and control of methanol concentration in cultures of Mut+, Mut- and MutS recombinant Pichia pastoris clones.

Thiols are compounds that have an active (-SH) functional group that participates in several biochemical reactions. The foremost potential therapeutic benefit of TTI-0102, is as the best-in-class method of generating the most important intracellular antioxidant - glutathione.

TTI-0102 is classified as a prodrug because its active moiety has been previously approved and is only biologically activated after oral administration. As a result, TTI-0102 can utilize the accelerated 505(b)(2) regulatory pathway in the United States and its equivalent in Europe, saving significant time and cost.

Thiogenesis is initially targeting pediatric diseases with unmet medical needs, that have oxidative stress as a core component and for which there is no approved therapy. Name: CuraDrone
Description:
CuraDrone is developing a first-of-its-kind intratumoral biological therapy: a new way to drive cancer drugs deep inside solid tumors and to wake the immune system. 

We call it an immuno-active Bacterial-Drug Conjugate.

How it works: 
CuraDrone uses self-propelled, magnetically guided bacteria, our Bacterial Drones, to carry a cancer drug already used in approved treatments deep into hard-to-reach tumor regions, including the oxygen-poor core that ordinary injections and body-wide treatments miss. It changes where the cancer drug goes, not what kills the cancer cell, and it also triggers a local immune response inside the tumor. After an intratumoral injection, the Bacterial Drones are guided by our PolarTrak system, a 3D magnetic guidance device working far below MRI field levels, for about 30 minutes to actively distribute the drug across the tumor.

The problems we target: cancers that no longer respond to standard treatments, where tumors keep returning after chemotherapy, radiation, or surgery has failed or is no longer suitable; cancer drugs that cannot reach far enough, because even a direct injection spreads poorly through dense tissue and leaves the low-oxygen core, where resistant cells survive, untreated; and surgery or radiation that have reached their limits, since they can cause lasting damage to healthy tissue and function and often cannot be repeated.

The cancers we target first are accessible, high-unmet-need tumors suited to image-guided local treatment: head and neck (such as recurrent disease), pelvic (prostate, rectal, and vulvar), abdominal (such as locally advanced, non-operable pancreatic cancer), and cutaneous (skin) metastases.

CuraDrone is an investigational technology and is not yet approved for commercial use. Preclinical results support progression toward human clinical trials.

Description:

The debilitating symptoms of opioid withdrawal affect all users, not just those who suffer with opioid use disorder. Current interventions to treat opioid withdrawal symptoms rely on long-acting opioid medications that affect normal nervous system function, creating a vicious cycle of treating opioid withdrawal with more opioids. Non-opioid pharmacological options for treating withdrawal are limited, have proven to be largely ineffective, and are known to cause serious side effects. 

Consequently, less than 30% of patients on opioid replacement therapies achieve abstinence, creating a huge unmet need for millions of people all over the world. Having safe and effective interventions that reduce withdrawal can break the cycle of opioid use.

TelomEYE is a company working on ophthalmic treatments to prevent and improve age-related ophthalmologic disorders such as presbyopia, cataracts and macular degeneration, each of which is a significant medical need.

It is a fact that everyone over the age of 40s eventually faces the need for reading glasses.

Starting in our late 30s, daily use of TelomEYE could remove or delay the necessity of reading glasses at later stages of life. Patients with dry eye syndrome which is a very common health problem may have beneficial effects as well.

TelomEYE is a privately held Canadian ophthalmology & biotech company founded in September 2021 by ophthalmologists Iskender Alkin Solmaz MD, Isilay Kavadarli MD and entrepreneur Kubilay Turkmen in Ontario, Canada. 

TelomEYE Pharmaceuticals Corporation has completed successful $1 million USD post-seed funding round, valuing the company at $10 million USD. With this financing, TelomEYE will be able to complete phase I & II human studies for their novel, patented therapy in ophthalmology. This therapy could be the start of a new era for treating many ophthalmologic age-related disorders including presbyopia, cataracts and macular degeneration.

Name: Cytinnov Biotechnologies Ltd.
Description:
In Cytinnov Biotechnologies, we provide a cell-manufacturing process optimization service on a contract basis to biotechnology companies in the regenerative medicine field, in order to lower the cost of goods of their novel cell-based therapies.

Cell-based therapies are poised to revolutionize healthcare, in Alberta and around the world. Promising to cure chronic diseases, and fully repair damaged tissues and organs, demand for these treatments will be tremendous – as will the costs. While the first few cell-based treatments have entered the Canadian health care market, the massive price tag serves as a bottleneck for the uptake of treatments by doctors, patents and the government. In some cases, the cost of goods alone for cell manufacturing is estimated to be in the tens and even hundreds of thousands of dollars per dose per patient. Effective, curative treatments may not see the light of day if they are not economically viable. The cost of cell manufacturing must come down to make cell therapies accessible.

In Cytinnov Biotechnologies, we fill this need by providing cell manufacturing process optimization services on a contract basis. Over the past several years, we have engineered a biomedical platform integrating scalable cell culture, advanced statistical methods, Machine Learning, and robotic systems to systematically optimize cell manufacturing processes, making them cheaper, faster, and more robust. To our knowledge, we are the first company in the world to offer this service. A team of innovators, scientists and entrepreneurs, we are excited to take on the first mover advantage, and are providing optimization services to our first customer this fall. 

Let’s make cell therapies accessible and revolutionize the future of healthcare!

Our primary goal is to stay connected to our community of researchers, and to meet their needs. We’ll do what it takes to tailor our work to your goals and limitations.

> Niche projects – We specialize in protocol optimization and custom applications – we’re not afraid to push current technology to the limits to meet your needs. The DSC is a beta site for many of our chemistry suppliers, allowing us to stay at the cutting edge of technology.

> Input flexibility – Where other providers may reject projects for failing to meet input requirements, our selection of methods allows success from a wide variety of inputs.

> Budget realism – We always do our best to tailor our protocols and work with suppliers to give you the most data at the lowest cost. Let us know the budget you’re working with, and we’ll scale projects or split sequencing runs to get you the data you want within your budget.

> Fast turnaround – We always work hard to keep turnaround time under ten business days for user-prepared libraries, and under eighteen for projects requiring full library preparation. But if you have an urgent upcoming deadline, let us know, and we’ll do our best to meet it!

> Collaboration – Working with us can be as hands-on or hands-off as you want. We offer project consultations, data interpretation, and in-person training for your staff and students – just ask us.

> Outreach: We also collaborate with local instructors in NGS and -omics courses; contact us about academic outreach.

To engender precision medicine in preclinical research an accessible reality.

This initiative is designed to establish the clinical, operational, and regulatory foundation required to bring continuously updating precision oncology into real-world care.

It is commonly accepted that the root of these tumor mutations is a selective pressure from these same biologics.  Treatment relapse from PCa therapies results in more aggressive disease known as castrate resistant PCa (CRPC), where the therapeutic options are almost non-existent.  

Currently, GNR is in the pre-clinical stages assessing a nanoformulation for the treatment of PCa.  

GNR’s nanotherapeutic platform employs a physical-directed based treatment approach through tumor ablation, thereby circumventing the failures biologics.    By harnessing the inherent physical properties of MWCNTs by differentiating itself with the following characteristics: 1. Conversion of light energy to generate extreme heat; 2. Easy functionalization of different tumor targeting molecules; 3. Excellent and safe systemic delivery properties without toxic or off-target effects.   The placement of these particles at the tumor site and upon exposure to laser light would dissipate an extreme radius of heat thus, causing complete photothermal ablation of the cancerous lesion.

The advantage of GNR’s nanotherapeutics technology is that provides an unchallenged therapeutic modality for treating PCa.

DPSCs are mesenchymal stem cells uniquely recognized for their capacity to differentiate into tissue types including bone, cartilage, nerves, cardiac cells, and even hepatocytes, making them an exceptionally versatile resource for tissue regeneration and repair.

The benefits of DPSC banking are strongly supported by scientific literature (1). Furthermore, cryogenic biobanking preserves stem cell “stemness” and potency for decades, ensuring DPSCs remain viable and ready for future medical breakthroughs.

Regenesis Biotech’s genetic screening services further enable clients to gain actionable insights into their genetic health risks, guiding proactive healthcare decisions and providing tailored recommendations. 

By banking younger stem cells—known for stronger renewal and regenerative capability—alongside genetic insights, Regenesis Biotech provides families and professionals a powerful combination for long-term health protection and personalized medical possibilities.

Name: Garde Bioscience
Description:
Prostate cancer is the second most common cancer in men worldwide. 1 in 8 men will be diagnosed in their lifetime,  yet the primary screening tool we use, the PSA test, generates false positives 75% of the time. Nearly 70% of patients end up overtreated, undergoing procedures they didn't need, with complications that can be permanent.
Garde Bioscience is building a better way.
We've developed a non-invasive, urine-based prostate cancer risk assessment test that analyzes exosomal small non-coding RNA (sncRNA) biomarkers using a supervised machine learning algorithm. The result: clinically actionable risk stratification (low, moderate, or elevated) delivered in as little as 24 hours, for a fraction of the cost of current alternatives.
Unlike existing tests that require invasive blood draws or biopsy tissue, our test starts with a urine sample. Unlike in-house laboratory tests that can't scale, our test is designed from day one to be licensed to reference labs, making it accessible through existing clinical infrastructure worldwide.
We will be conducting validation and clinical studies in collaboration with the Vancouver Prostate Centre.  We are currently raising a $4M pre-seed round.

Description:
Celebrities like Steve Jobs and Aretha Franklin, both diagnosed with rare neuroendocrine tumours, would have been among those to benefit from work we are doing with funding awarded through a 2023 Terry Fox New Frontiers Program Project Grant.  This funded work will help to address what is currently an unmet need for these patients. Neuroendocrine tumours are often diagnosed late and current treatment options are poor. Moreover, the incidence rate is growing and our understanding of this disease needs improvement.  This multidisciplinary, pan-Canadian team aims to:

1) Improve our understanding of these deadly tumours and identify new treatment avenues by diving into the role of a signalling pathway known as miR-181 in three major types of NETs: pancreatic NETs (PanNETs), therapy-induced neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC).
2) Focus on understanding and, if possible, delaying or preventing NEPC, which typically results in death within two years of diagnosis. This project centres on studying the role of circular RNA in driving the transformation of this cancer and understanding how this transformation results in resistance to advanced androgen-receptor targeting therapies.
3) Advance therapeutic strategies in neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), a rare and aggressive form of cancer that occurs when cancerous neuroendocrine cells spread to other parts of the body. A preclinical “basket” study is proposed to efficiently explore therapeutic vulnerabilities that are common across NECs/NETs.
4) Improve diagnostic pathways and patient monitoring using an innovative approach called “liquid biopsies.” First, they will develop a “universal NET liquid biopsy” to detect any neuroendocrine tumour.  
5) Use advanced techniques such as specialized animal models and microfluidics to test the effectiveness of various therapeutic approaches and test a wide variety of therapies and tumours regardless of disease site.

Name: Pavonis Diagnostics Inc.
Description:
Pavonis Diagnostics is developing VICA (Visual Interference Color Assay), a disruptive optical biosensing platform that combines binding analysis, assay development and biomolecule capture in one fast, flexible system. Using nanostructured anodized alumina thin films, VICA detects molecular interactions through measurable optical changes and can assess binding in solution or on a surface using minimal sample and reagents. The platform supports screening, specificity testing, conditional binding, matrix tolerance, pH-dependent interactions, off-rate challenges, isotyping, purification and recovery of biomolecules.

VICA can generate preliminary results in about one hour, support multiplexed testing and operate without the cost and complexity of traditional SPR, BLI or spectrophotometric instruments. It is designed for biotechnology companies, antibody and peptide developers, academic laboratories, CROs, diagnostics developers, veterinary health companies and computational protein-design teams that need experimental feedback.

Pavonis is initially offering VICA through development and testing services, followed by device and assay-kit offerings. Potential markets include antibody discovery, peptide engineering, biosimilar characterization, biomarker testing, infectious disease, oncology, therapeutic monitoring, agriculture and animal health. By connecting rapid measurements with AI-guided molecular design, VICA can help users test more candidates, explore more conditions and get to market faster!

Name: Drystill Holdings Inc.
Description:
Drystill is a developer and supplier of advanced, chemical separation technology.  The company has developed a revolutionary, low-energy, separation process which, if applied to biofuel production, offers opportunities to significantly increase yield, and reduce operating and capital costs.   This technical breakthrough can lead to a paradigm shift in biofuel production methods in the future.

Drystill's technology can be applied to 1st, 2nd and 3rd generation biofuels, and to existing and new plants.  The technology scales readily upwards and downwards to meet unique user needs.  It may also be applied in other industries such as food and beverages, and specialty chemicals.

At heart of Drystill's technology is a proprietary , novel apparatus called a stripper/ absorption module ("SAM").  A SAM performs two important functions in the mainstream, production process.   Firstly, it continuously removes ethanol from a weak  fermentation broth - as it is produced - without harming the enzymes and yeast.  Secondly, it transfers fermented ethanol to a non-fouling, absorbent fluid, from which it can be more economically distilled.

Users of Drystill's technology will enjoy substantial improvements in their economic returns.

We support the development of recombinant cytokines, vaccine antigens, diagnostic enzymes, and RNA polymerases used in immunotherapy, molecular diagnostics, and gene technologies. We work with health-focused biotech companies, diagnostic developers, and labs in need of early validation.

Produire plus et produire mieux sont des enjeux majeurs des décennies à venir afin d’être capable de nourrir une population mondiale estimée à plus de 10 milliards d’individus en 2050 dont 25% sur le continent africain. Cette croissance de la population mondiale entrainera une augmentation de la demande en protéines animales. 


Actuellement, les animaux se nourrissent de farine et d’huile de poisson, du maïs, de soja et autres céréales, mais ces ressources sont limitées. Les stocks de poisson sont actuellement exploités à leur maximum et la production de farine de poisson atteindra un plafond de production. De plus, la grande majorité de la production agricole est destinée à la poubelle.

Ces produits sont des alternatives durables au soja et à la farine de poisson dans l’alimentation animale. Notre engrais organique riche en azote est un co-produit notre ferme qui permet d’enrichir nos sols et joue un rôle important dans la valorisation de la culture biologique.


Chez NEXFID, nous prenons à cœur le changement climatique et l’alimentation humaine. Nous croyons profondément à la possibilité de reconstruire nos habitudes alimentaires au tour des enjeux climatiques. Nous redonnons à l’insecte, son pouvoir de la chaîne alimentaire.

Name: Crop Defenders Ltd
Description:
Crop Defenders was developed and devised by the founder, Dr. Ishtiaq Rao. Before Dr. Rao was “Dr.” Rao, he saw how much money there was to be made in pesticide sales, so he decided to study entomology. At this time, agricultural pest control strategies were entirely based on pesticides. One year into his entomology program, Dr. Ishtiaq Rao would witness chemical sprays that caused birds to fall from the air, dead. Some time later, he visited hospitals and witnessed people who were very sick as a result of rampant pesticide use. He used to see people come to the villages for fresh air, now the villagers themselves were dying for fresh air. It was after seeing all this that he made the decision to never sell chemical pesticides and made the life-changing decision to get into biologicals.

Dr. Rao committed his life to finding the best biological solutions to help growers. He has spent countless hours working in and on farms, and helping growers see first-hand how much more effective biologicals are to producing more profitable and higher yielding crops. He was so passionate and felt so convicted of this, that decades ago he bet one grower $10k that biological control would work better than pesticides at reducing his pest problem. It did. And Crop Defenders took flight. It is this passion that has fueled Crop Defenders’ success and growth.

Description:

We host talks, expert seminar series, workshops, active learning opportunities and much more! We aim to teach, train, and spark curiosity about these new fields in science that are emerging as this century’s most important scope. The University of British Columbia Okanagan curriculum lacks a focus in these areas which is why we want to bring these opportunities to students and researchers from every discipline, regardless of year or major!

While we host lab-related activities and workshops that are open to everyone as a Club, our main objective each year is to form an iGEM Competition Team on campus and participate in the annual International Genetically Engineered Machine Competition, held in Paris! Started in 2003 by MIT, the Competition has now expanded to hold over 350 teams from 46 different countries, and is the largest international synthetic biology competition in the world! iGEMers have the opportunity to spend their summer developing a synthetic biology research project, working in our Wet Lab, Dry Lab, Human Practices and Finance subgroups and meeting with experts worldwide! Some examples of projects include designing a carbon-negative light source using bacteria, synthesizing biodegradable plastics, creating diagnostic tests for wastewater contaminants and much more! This is your opportunity to expand your curriculum, learn incredible things, make great connections, and create projects in the pursuit of a better world. 

Welcome to iGEM!

Our platform, Elyra, converts patient tumor genomic data into ranked neoantigen candidates for personalized mRNA vaccine design — in days, not months, at a fraction of the cost of conventional approaches.

The Problem We Are Solving
Personalized cancer vaccines work by identifying mutations in a patient's tumor that produce protein fragments — called neoantigens — which the immune system can recognize and attack. A tumor may carry hundreds of mutations, but only a handful will produce neoantigens capable of triggering a meaningful immune response. A vaccine can carry only 10 to 20 candidates. Choosing the right ones is a computational problem, and the current clinical standard has not kept pace with what the science now tells us about immunogenicity.

The dominant tool in clinical neoantigen prediction ranks candidates primarily by binding affinity — how strongly a peptide binds to the patient's immune presentation molecules. But binding affinity is only one of several factors that determine whether a neoantigen will actually trigger an immune response. Is the gene active in the patient's tumor? If not, the mutation cannot produce a neoantigen, regardless of binding strength. Does the mutation make the peptide look sufficiently foreign compared to the normal version? Is the mutation positioned where T cells can recognize it? Published research has established that these factors matter significantly. The TESLA consortium — 36 research groups with experimentally confirmed immunogenicity labels — identified five key parameters governing neoantigen immunogenicity. Yet in clinical practice, most vaccine trials still rank by binding affinity alone.

Our proprietary technology focus on the dual functions of pentamidine on controlling the function of a DNA repair enzyme – endo-exonuclease (EE:Trmt2) and specific targets anti-inflammatory/Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) binding.

The EE is found in large amounts in cancer cells and its function is to repair DNA breaks that occur when cancer cells proliferate. Blocking this enzyme would cut off cancer growth. Pentamidine is known to be active on cancer cells. The effectiveness and significance of DNA repair process in medicine has most recently been exemplified in 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

The effect of pentamidine as potential anti-inflammatory agent is well documented6,7. However, its development for anti-inflammation application is limited by its cytotoxic effect. The research carried out by this laboratory concerns the development of computer vision techniques and image analysis algorithms for microscopy and neurophotonics. The goal of LINUM is to better understand the organization of the brain by exploiting optical imaging modalities and advanced methods in data analysis.

The main research projects of this laboratory focus on neurophotonics and the analysis of biomedical images. In particular, we use several imaging modalities (serial histology, optical coherence microscopy, 2-photon microscopy, diffusion MRI, etc.) to image whole ex vivo mouse brains. The goal is to better understand the organization of white matter fiber crossings in order to improve the performance of tractography algorithms used in clinics with diffusion MRI data. In addition, these research projects aim to combine microscopy and artificial intelligence to assist microscope users and facilitate the discovery of information for biomedical research and diagnostics. This line of research is called augmented microscopy

- A blockade of cell division at the late G2/M boundary, a site in the cell cycle that is believed to be optimal for radiation-induced damage.

- A slowing of the rate of tumor proliferation, which enables normalization of the tumor neo-vasculature. The result is better oxygenation and more efficient drug delivery.

- Formation of a more complete tumor vasculature, which reduces the poorly formed, disorganized vascular sites where metastatic cells penetrate the circulatory system.
